newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 16.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in April.
* USX-Marathon Group and Ashland Inc will combine some of their oil businesses, creating a refining powerhouse.
* Hewlett-Packard Co said weak sales of key computer and printer lines had led to a disappointing quarter.
* General Motors Corp is pushing its parts suppliers around the world to hold warranty-repair costs below specified levels or risk being penalised.
* A judge has ruled that Viacom Inc violated a partnership with Seagram Co Ltd.
* Dow Chemical Co said it would pay $900 million to buy Eli Lilly and Co's 40 percent stake in their agricultural chemicals joint venture, known as Dow Elanco.
* Airbus Industrie has a $1.5 billion deal to supply jets to Chinese airlines.
* The Dow Jones Industrials index rose 47.39 to a record 7333.55 points.
* Kmart Corp beat expectations with its quarterly earnings, while Gap Inc and Saks Holdings Inc were in line with analysts' expectations.
* United Airlines plans to launch a new ad campaign that apologises to passengers for the sad state of affairs in air travel.
* Glaxo Wellcome Plc received FDA approval for its Zyban, a prescription drug to help smokers quit.
* Junk-bond funds are bringing in record amounts of new cash, but some managers warn that junk bonds are starting to get pricey.
* The Internal Revenue Service released a blueprint for its troubled computer modernisation programme.
* The Small Business Administration said it would run out of money in its loan programme before the end of the September 30 fiscal year.
* Heard on the Street: A recent study suggests that small investors aren't as bad at stock picking as many people think. They may be worse.
* Credit markets: U.S. Treasury eked out further gains as somewhat contradictory economic data failed to settle the question of whether the Federal Reserve needs to raise interest rates next week.
